notes.title: Update 1.0.5.1 - Steam Achievements & New Manual Formats
notes.content:
This update brings Steam Achievements to FREM Sprite32! It also includes a handful of other updates and additions including:

[list]
[*] Checkmarks/X's on the challenges stickies when you pass/fail tasks when running validate (F4).
[*] The User's Manual is now available in PDF and .doc formats for viewing outside of the game. You can find buttons to open the new formats from the manual navbar (Press F1 to open the in-game manual, the buttons are on the bottom right).
[/list]
Have fun unlocking the new achievements, and be sure to leave feedback and report any issues in the forums!

Happy Coding,

John
Negative(-11) Games Division

notes.title: Upcoming Updates & Additions for FREM Sprite32!
notes.content:
Howdy!

As the new year has begun, I wanted to give an update for the roadmap for FREM Sprite32! going forward. After releasing the game in October, I pushed several quality of life updates and small fixes based on the initial feedback, so thanks to everyone who participated in the community discussions, left a review, and/or messaged me directly with their feedback! After taking a much needed break during the December/January holiday stretch, I'm ready to get back to working on a few new additions and improvements. 

Here's what I've got planned in upcoming builds:

[list]
[*] Steam Achievements. This is probably the most requested feature, and I aim to do it. It's a bit of work to come up with them and add them to the Steam back end, so this may take me a bit to finalize. I have several jotted down in a spreadsheet, but I still need to come up with more. I also need to revisit the Godot library I previously explored, to see if my build requirements have been resolved. I'll be digging into this in the coming weeks.
[*] Updates to the Manual, adding new formats to build directory. If you saw the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2065990/discussions/0/3722818378192986623/]portable manual discussion[/url], then you may already have found and read the PDF/.doc version of the FREM manual. A future build will include .doc and PDF versions as part of the game files. Additionally, while porting it over to those formats, I found a several typos/errors/etc. in the in-game manual that need correcting.
[*] General improvements, QoL fixes. There are several small fixes I have planned, which include things like tracking completed challenges and marking them on the UI, and supporting more mouse buttons.
[*] Standalone ROM player. Early during FREM development I had the idea to make a standalone FREMScript player, and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2065990/discussions/0/5533260453840096716/]some others have suggested it[/url]. There are some technical challenges to overcome, and I'm not 100% certain that it will see the light of day, but I do intend to spend some more time exploring it.
[/list]

So, when are these updates coming? The short answer is: when they're ready. I plan to do a build with some of the small QoL changes and manual additions toward the end of January, After that, my next delivery focus will be Steam achievements, whenever they are ready to go. Between now and then, if any new ideas come to light, I'll consider them.

Thanks for reading, and stay tuned for more FREM updates down the road. 

Feedback is highly valued, so drop by the Discussions page and share your requests, thoughts, screenshots, and creations!

Cheers,

John 
Negative(-11) Games Division

notes.title: Update 1.0.4.0 - Introducing Mouse Support
notes.content:
I'm pleased to announce the latest update for Win/macOS which introduces mouse support for FREMScript programs. 

Take your Sprite32! programs to the next level with new built-in functions that output the mouse position and left and right button states. Be sure to check out the new SpriteMaker program in the software folder, which showcases the new mouse input features. Additionally, the manual has been updated to document the new functions with examples.

The latest build also includes a few minor bugfixes and QoL updates.

Here's the full change log for this update:

[h2]1.0.4.0[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added mouse support to FREMScript
[*] Updated manual Chapter 15: Input to document new mouse functions.
[*] Updated manual Appendix 5: Built-in functions to document new mouse functions.
[*] Added SpriteMaker 1.0 to software in order to demo mouse support
[*] General improvements to big screen view to block interactions with controls and editor hidden behind it.
[*] Updated manual "Add It" handler to insert code examples at cursor position.
[*] Applied minor fix in Settings Menu for macOS to mitigate lockup/blank screen when unchecking full screen
[/list]

notes.title: Making some optimizations to the Sprite & Grid Layers
notes.content:
This update makes a few improvements to how the game creates objects used by the Sprite and Grid layers. Under the hood, the game was previously creating a number of resources to support the rendering of the Grid and Sprite layers, even if the executed programs never used them. Now, resources will be allocated only when a program enables these layers, and freed when the Sprite32! is reset or power cycled. These changes should improve memory usage and CPU load when not using the Grid and Sprite layers in programs.

[h2]1.0.3.0[/h2]
[list]
[*] Improved object handling and rendering of the Grid Layer to reduce memory and cpu footprint
[*] Improved object handling and rendering of the Sprite Layer to reduce memory and cpu footprint
[*] Updates/Additions to some examples affected by sprite modifications.
[*] Added Pixel Painter 1.0 to the software folder
[/list]

tags.feature: Added Pixel Painter 1.0 to the software folder
